purpose: Progressively disclosed official resources and agent integrations for prax-teach visualization routes.

trust_levels.official-standard: Specification maintained by a standards body.
trust_levels.first-party-tool-docs: Official project documentation and source; no portable first-party agent integration is implied.
trust_levels.first-party-agent-integration: Skill, MCP, plugin, or agent surface maintained by the tool owner.
trust_levels.local-vetted: Workflow inspected on the source host; current availability must be probed and is not maintained by the target tool project.
trust_levels.community-unverified: Third-party integration requiring source, permission, dependency, and compatibility review.

selection_order: existing working tool in the lesson workspace
verified first-party skill, MCP, plugin, or CLI
small local adapter built from official documentation

tools.name: SVG
tools.summary: Standards-based editable vector format and the default for precise labelled lesson graphics.
tools.fallback: Author semantic SVG directly from the SVG specification; a wrapper is unnecessary.
verification: Parse XML and render in the target browser; inspect viewBox, fonts, labels, clipping, and paths.
Require title, description, accessible role, non-color cues, and a raster preview.

tools.name: Mermaid
tools.summary: Fast text-defined diagrams for modest processes and relationships.
tools.fallback: Use the official Mermaid grammar and CLI directly; step down to SVG or draw.io when layout is ambiguous.
verification: Render with the target Mermaid version and inspect labels, directions, edge crossings, and accessibility.
Split diagrams that exceed one screen.

tools.name: D2
tools.summary: Text-defined diagrams with selectable layout engines and strong styling.
tools.fallback: Use the official syntax and CLI; use SVG or Mermaid when D2 is unavailable.
verification: Compile with D2, record the layout engine, and inspect labels, routing, and hierarchy.

tools.name: Graphviz / DOT
tools.summary: Canonical graph layout suite; use DOT directly without requiring an agent wrapper.
tools.fallback: Write DOT from the official grammar and render with the appropriate layout engine.
verification: Run dot -V, compile to SVG, and inspect crossings, rank, clipping, labels, and chosen engine.

tools.name: draw.io / diagrams.net
tools.summary: Professional editable diagrams with a verified first-party MCP and native XML format.

install.command: codex plugin marketplace add jgraph/drawio-mcp && codex plugin add drawio@drawio

tools.fallback: Generate native .drawio XML from the official XML reference and open it in diagrams.net.
verification: Validate XML, reopen and edit the source, then inspect connectors, labels, layers, and export.
Prefer local rendering for private diagrams; record remote-service data egress.

tools.name: Vega-Lite
tools.summary: Declarative grammar for reproducible quantitative visualizations.

install.command: npx -p vega -p vega-lite vl2svg input.json > output.svg

tools.fallback: Author JSON against the official schema and use the official editor or CLI.
verification: Validate schema, render, and audit field types, scales, units, missingness, uncertainty, sample size, and provenance.

tools.name: Observable Plot
tools.summary: Concise JavaScript charting organized around composable marks.
tools.fallback: Use the official JavaScript API in plain HTML or a notebook.
verification: Render the actual DOM and inspect transforms, domains, axes, labels, source data, and static fallback.

tools.name: Apache ECharts
tools.summary: Feature-rich interactive charting with declarative option objects.
tools.fallback: Author the official option object directly; use SVG rendering and a static capture.
verification: Render and resize in a browser; audit scales, data, ARIA, decals, keyboard behavior, and static fallback.

tools.name: Matplotlib
tools.summary: Mature Python plotting for reproducible scientific and static figures.
tools.fallback: Use a Python script or notebook and save SVG or PNG.
verification: Execute headlessly with pinned inputs and inspect axes, units, uncertainty, missingness, and exported pixels.

tools.name: Plotly
tools.summary: Interactive plotting for Python and JavaScript with standalone HTML delivery.
tools.fallback: Use Plotly Express or graph_objects and export standalone HTML; avoid frozen plotly-latest CDN aliases.
verification: Validate the figure schema, browser interaction, scales, provenance, and static fallback; note rasterized WebGL traces.

tools.name: Altair
tools.summary: Python interface that produces inspectable Vega-Lite specifications.
tools.fallback: Generate Vega-Lite JSON or HTML directly from Python.
verification: Execute Python, validate the generated Vega-Lite spec, and inspect data, scales, missingness, and provenance.

tools.name: ggplot2
tools.summary: R grammar-of-graphics plotting with strong statistical workflows.
tools.fallback: Use an R script and ggsave() to SVG, PNG, or PDF.
verification: Run non-interactively and inspect factor order, scales, units, missingness, uncertainty, and export.

tools.name: Excalidraw
tools.summary: Appropriately informal diagrams for mental models and collaborative refinement.
tools.fallback: Author .excalidraw JSON against the official schema and open it in Excalidraw.
verification: Parse, reopen, and re-edit; inspect arrow bindings, labels, overlap, SVG export, and text fallback.

tools.name: Kroki
tools.summary: Rendering gateway for many diagram languages; it supplies no diagram grammar of its own.
tools.fallback: Use HTTP POST or the CLI against a self-hosted server and validate the underlying source language.
verification: Render locally for privacy and determinism; validate the source grammar and inspect the returned diagram.

tools.name: PlantUML
tools.summary: Text-defined UML and technical diagrams.
tools.fallback: Use .puml text with the official JAR or server; Kroki is a secondary renderer.
verification: Render with a pinned JAR and inspect warnings, labels, layout, and output portability.

tools.name: Structurizr
tools.summary: Semantic architecture model with multiple consistent views and a verified first-party MCP.
tools.fallback: Use Structurizr DSL plus the official CLI or playground and export to Mermaid or PlantUML.
verification: Validate and inspect DSL, view keys, model consistency, and each rendered export.

tools.name: Penrose
tools.summary: Constraint-based mathematical diagram system separating domain, substance, and style.
tools.fallback: Use the official editor or Domain, Substance, and Style sources with Roger.
verification: Compile and optimize, pin the variation string, sample layouts, and inspect semantic constraints.

tools.name: HTML
tools.summary: Standards-based semantic surface for every prax-teach lesson.
tools.fallback: Write standards-based HTML directly; an MCP is optional.
verification: Run an HTML validator and test semantics, keyboard order, accessible names, responsive layout, and print.

tools.name: CSS
tools.summary: Standards-based styling and responsive layout for lesson visuals.
tools.fallback: Use native CSS and the official grammar directly.
verification: Validate CSS and test screenshots, zoom, contrast, reduced motion, print, and narrow widths.

tools.name: JavaScript
tools.summary: Standards-based browser interaction without requiring a framework.
tools.fallback: Write standard JavaScript and execute it in the lesson browser.
verification: Check console errors, deterministic state, event cleanup, keyboard paths, and target-browser support.

tools.name: Canvas 2D
tools.summary: Browser-native immediate-mode raster drawing; unrelated to local dcanvas or JSON Canvas skills.
tools.fallback: Use CanvasRenderingContext2D directly; do not route to dcanvas or JSON Canvas.
verification: Test device-pixel ratio, resize, hit testing, deterministic frames, screenshots, and semantic text fallback.

tools.name: WebGL
tools.summary: Standards-based GPU rendering when Canvas or SVG cannot handle the required scale.
tools.fallback: Use official WebGL and shader grammar directly, or Three.js when scene abstraction is useful.
verification: Check shader compile/link logs, gl errors, WebGL2 support, context loss, performance, screenshots, and static fallback.

tools.name: React Flow
tools.summary: React toolkit for node-edge systems the learner must manipulate.

install.note: Import the package CSS and give the parent explicit dimensions.

tools.fallback: Read the official llms.txt and API documentation, then write React code directly.
verification: Test stable IDs, serialization, callbacks, keyboard accessibility, container sizing, interaction, and screenshot.

tools.name: Three.js
tools.summary: High-level 3D scene library over WebGL.
tools.fallback: Use the official module and API docs directly; WebGL is the lower-level fallback.
verification: Pin core and addon versions, await assets, inspect console and renderer.info, dispose resources, and test pixel ratio and poster fallback.

tools.name: D3
tools.summary: Low-level composable data visualization when declarative chart tools are insufficient.
tools.fallback: Use official D3 modules directly; do not install a wrapper merely to gain a skill.
verification: Audit domains, scales, axes, missingness, uncertainty, sample size, provenance, DOM, screenshot, and table fallback.

tools.name: Cytoscape.js
tools.summary: Browser graph visualization and analysis; distinct from Cytoscape Desktop.
tools.fallback: Use the official JavaScript API; use headless mode for semantic graph assertions.
verification: Assert node and edge IDs/counts, layout and styles, interactions, screenshots, and an accessible list.

tools.name: Sigma.js
tools.summary: WebGL graph rendering over Graphology for large networks.
tools.fallback: Use stable v3 documentation and Graphology directly; do not silently adopt the v4 alpha.
verification: Validate graph IDs, container dimensions, WebGL, picking, camera behavior, performance, screenshot, and accessible list.

tools.name: deck.gl
tools.summary: Layered WebGL visualization for large geospatial and spatial datasets.
tools.fallback: Use official layer APIs directly; use Canvas or a static map when scale does not require WebGL.
verification: Audit coordinates, projection, aligned package versions, WebGL2, picking, lifecycle tests, and golden images.

tools.name: Rive
tools.summary: Authored vector state machines and interactive animations.
tools.fallback: Use the official runtime with an authored .riv file and exact artboard and state-machine names.
verification: Test asset load, names, inputs, data binding, resize, cleanup, CSP/WASM, reduced motion, and poster fallback.

tools.name: dotLottie
tools.summary: Portable Lottie packaging and runtime with verified first-party MCP and skill options.
tools.fallback: Author or play .lottie using the official runtime and specification without MCP.
verification: Validate manifest IDs, themes, markers, renderer, seek/loop events, reduced motion, accessibility, and poster.

tools.name: Manim Community
tools.summary: Preferred Python film route for precise mathematical and technical transformations; pin 0.21.0 at first use.

install.command: uv init manimations && cd manimations && uv add manim==0.21.0

tools.fallback: Use the official Python API or Manim Docker image; choose static SVG when motion is unnecessary.
verification: Run manim --version and manim checkhealth; draft-render and inspect first, proof, and final frames plus equations.
tools.licensing: MIT code; example assets can have separate rights. Modern Manim uses PyAV internally, so external FFmpeg is not a core prerequisite.

tools.name: Motion Canvas
tools.summary: Historical TypeScript/TSX animation entry retained for provenance; do not route new Teach Pro Max work here.
tools.fallback: Use the official TS API; retain a frame sequence if encoding is unavailable, or step down to SVG.
verification: Render image sequences, inspect first/proof/final frames, encode explicitly, and validate duration and FPS.

tools.name: Remotion
tools.summary: Legacy React-video adapter retained for provenance; use HyperFrames or Manim for new Teach Pro Max work.
tools.fallback: Use HyperFrames for general film or Manim for mathematical and algorithmic film.
verification: Inspect frame 0, proof frames, and final frame in Studio; render and validate streams with ffprobe.
tools.licensing: Source-available with usage-dependent licensing. Check current pricing for organizations. Do not recommend the deprecated Remotion MCP.

tools.name: HyperFrames
tools.summary: First-party agent-oriented HTML video system with an optionally discoverable local skill suite.
tools.fallback: Use npx and the official HTML composition contract; use deterministic Docker rendering if the host renderer fails.
verification: Run doctor, lint, mandatory check, keyframe/snapshot inspection, preview, render, and ffprobe.
tools.licensing: Apache-2.0. Refresh installed workflow skills before relying on them.

tools.name: OpenAI Image Generation
tools.summary: First-party generated imagery for appearance—not authoritative labels, charts, or topology.

install.command: No install when image_gen is available

tools.fallback: Use the official API for batches; use SVG or diagrams for exact semantics.
verification: Retain prompt, model, rights, date, original, and hash; inspect at target size, OCR text, fact-check claims, and add alt text.
tools.licensing: Record reference-image rights and identify synthetic media when it could be mistaken for documentary evidence.

tools.name: Wikimedia Commons
tools.summary: Sourced media with machine-readable per-file licensing and provenance.
tools.fallback: Use the file page and Attribution Generator; choose another asset when rights are ambiguous.
verification: Compare API metadata with file page and revision history; retain permanent URL, retrieval date, and SHA-1.
tools.licensing: Varies per asset. Record creator, exact licence/version/link, attribution, ShareAlike duties, modifications, and other rights.

tools.name: Unsplash
tools.summary: Contemporary photography with specific licence and API attribution duties.
tools.fallback: Use Wikimedia Commons when explicit Creative Commons or public-domain licensing is preferable.
verification: Resolve full metadata, verify attribution links and download event, and inspect the final crop.
tools.licensing: Record photo ID, photographer, profile/source URLs, retrieval date, transforms, and people/logo/art/property rights. Do not use the discontinued Source service.

tools.name: FFmpeg
tools.summary: Production backend rather than a visualization route; used to encode and verify media.
tools.fallback: Use the framework-native renderer, a frame sequence, or a deterministic container.
verification: Capture ffmpeg -version configuration and use ffprobe to verify duration, FPS, dimensions, pixel format, codecs, audio, and sample frames.
tools.licensing: Enabled GPL or nonfree components change obligations; --enable-nonfree builds are not redistributable.
